premise.spark: In a remote Swiss mountain village the one man who could prove the district doctor covered up a fatal malpractice 20 years ago dies in a fall, and now lies awaiting the death certificate that same doctor must sign.
premise.central_question: Can a man whom chance offers the means to bury his guilt for good resist the offer — or does the very chance to make it final force a second, worse crime?
premise.thesis: Guilt administered for twenty years instead of confessed turns every accident of the world into a verdict the guilty man can no longer escape, because he is the only one who could still recognize it as an accident.
premise.why_this_author: Duerrenmatt's obsession: justice possible only by grotesque chance; the institution (the death certificate, the file) as the trap that closes on its keeper.

facts.secret: 20 years ago forged Klara Vogel's death certificate to 'Herzversagen'
facts.trait: conflates record-keeping with absolution; dry, procedural speech

arc.want: close the Aebischer case quickly and keep his standing
arc.need: to confess rather than administer his guilt
arc.trajectory: does not change; hardens into his own system until it becomes his prison

facts.reputation: womanizer and debtor; owed money to the innkeeper and to Rutz
facts.death: fall of ~12m into the Chrachen, no autopsy performed
facts.identifier: scar on the chin from an old axe injury

facts.habit: double-underlines his notes; believes in procedure

facts.trait: unsentimental, exact memory; states the unspeakable plainly

facts.relation: old friend of Stettler; Melchior owed him 300 francs privately

facts.cover: Stettler forged her death certificate to 'Herzversagen'

world_facts.setting: Lauenegg, a remote village in Graubuenden, Switzerland
world_facts.loc:chrachen: a gorge south of the village; the stream freezes greenish in winter; site of Melchior's fall
world_facts.loc:eichenschrank: the oak filing cabinet where case files are archived
world_facts.formula: 'Herzversagen, vermutlich beim Sturz' — the reused death-certificate formula, identical across both cases

timeline.event: Klara Vogel dies; Stettler forges her death certificate to 'Herzversagen'
Melchior Aebischer falls to his death in the Chrachen (~12m)
Dorfwehr retrieves the body; Stettler declares heart failure/fall; Feuz interviews on site
Berta identifies the body; Feuz files the certificate without an autopsy
Feuz finds the 20-year-old Vogel file with the identical formula and Stettler's signature
Berta asks whether it is the same as the Vogel case
Stettler nearly confesses to Rutz, breaks off, flees into procedure; Rutz withholds a blessing
Feuz closes the case as accident; Stettler co-signs the report
Stettler files the Aebischer record beside the Vogel file and locks the cabinet

motifs.desc: the identical death-certificate phrase recurs across both cases
the oak filing cabinet as order-as-concealment; opens and closes the story
the gorge as the indifferent site that 'takes' what the village discards

promises.desc: Berta's unanswered 'is it the same as the Vogel?' — deliberately never resolved
Rutz's withheld blessing pays off as the final wordless verdict
